Title: FOOD HYGIENE — GENERAL PRINCIPLES — CODE OF PRACTICE (Third Revision)
Scope: Covers essential principles of food hygiene throughout the food chain, from primary production through the final consumer, to ensure food is safe and suitable for human consumption.
Material: Food-contact surfaces/materials should be non-toxic in intended use; durable and easy to maintain/clean where necessary.
Performance: Hygienic design and construction; contamination minimized; appropriate maintenance, cleaning/disinfection; protection against pests; suitable temperature/humidity controls where appropriate.
Testing: Sanitation effectiveness may be verified by audit, pre-operational inspection and, where appropriate, microbiological sampling of environment and food-contact surfaces.
Sampling: Where appropriate, microbiological sampling of environment and food-contact surfaces; periodic verification and review.
Acceptance Criteria: Requirements are applied according to safety/suitability and risk assessment; HACCP or FSMS approach is recommended where possible.
Marking: Lot identification: each food container should be permanently marked to identify producer and lot. Pre-packaged foods should carry clear handling/storage/use instructions.
Application: Food hygiene across the food chain, including production, processing, handling, storage, transport and final consumption.
Evidence / Section: Clause 1, p.1; Clauses 5.0–5.3, pp.3–5; Clauses 7.5 and 10.1–10.3, pp.10–11 (PDF pp.3–13).

Title: FOOD SAFETY MANAGEMENT — REQUIREMENTS FOR GOOD HYGIENE PRACTICES
Scope: Covers requirements for good hygiene practices throughout the food chain, including primary production through the final consumer, to ensure food is safe and suitable for human consumption.
Material: Establishment structures should use durable, easy-to-maintain/clean materials; food-contact surfaces should have suitable hygienic properties and no toxic effect in intended use.
Performance: Requires a documented and maintained hygiene system; control of contamination; hygienic production, handling, storage and transport; suitable establishment design and facilities; personal hygiene and sanitation controls.
Testing: Sanitation systems shall be monitored for effectiveness and periodically verified by audit/pre-operational inspection; microbiological sampling may be used where appropriate.
Sampling: Where appropriate, microbiological sampling of environment and food-contact surfaces as part of monitoring effectiveness.
Acceptance Criteria: Food business operator shall demonstrate responsibility for safe/suitable food and identify applicable statutory/regulatory requirements; hygiene activities shall be defined, documented, implemented and maintained.
Application: Food businesses throughout the food chain, from primary production to final consumer.
Evidence / Section: Clause 1, p.1; Clauses 4.1–4.1.2, pp.1–2; Clause 5.1, p.4; Clause 5.4.5, p.14 (PDF pp.6–19).

Title: STREET FOOD VENDORS — FOOD SAFETY REQUIREMENTS
Scope: Lays down control check points with minimum requirements to ensure safe food; covers mobile and fixed food vendors serving prepared/raw food for human consumption.
Material: Raw materials shall conform to accepted national standards. Vending carts should use solid, rust/corrosion-resistant materials and be maintained clean and in good condition.
Dimensions: Working surfaces: at least 60–70 cm above ground. Transported drinking water: protected containers of at least 20 litre.
Performance: Inputs should be fresh and within expiry/best-before where applicable; food protected from contamination; raw/semi-cooked/cooked foods stored separately; vending location and cart kept hygienic; waste controlled.
Testing: Compliance is demonstrated through the control check points and applicable statutory/regulatory requirements; no separate product test programme is specified in the standard.
Acceptance Criteria: All applicable statutory/regulatory requirements shall be complied with and applicable control check points followed.
Marking: Ingredients identical in appearance shall be suitably identified/labelled.
Application: Mobile and fixed street-food vendors serving prepared/raw food for human consumption.
Evidence / Section: Clause 1, p.1; Clauses 3.1–3.4, pp.1–3; especially 3.4.1, 3.4.3 and 3.4.4 (PDF pp.6–8).

Title: WHOLE MILK POWDER — SPECIFICATION (Sixth Revision)
Scope: Prescribes requirements, methods of sampling and tests for whole milk powder.
Material: Product is obtained by partial removal of water from milk; product shall be free from added whey/whey preparations. Packaging includes food-grade flexible packs or clean/sound containers; bulk bags may be food-grade polyethylene.
Dimensions: Bulk packing may be 25 kg; food-grade polyethylene bag minimum thickness 0.05 mm. Retail pack quantities follow applicable Legal Metrology requirements.
Performance: Key requirements include moisture max 4.0%; total solids min 96.0%; milk fat ≥26.0% and <42.0%; milk protein in milk solids-not-fat min 34.0%; insolubility index max 2.0 ml; total ash max 7.3%; titratable acidity max 18.0; scorched particles max 15 mg/kg. Microbiological and contaminant limits are also specified.
Testing: Tests include moisture, fat, protein, insolubility index, total ash, titratable acidity, scorched particles, microbiological tests and contaminant/toxin tests using the referenced methods in Tables 1–3.
Sampling: Representative samples shall be drawn and tested as prescribed in Annex C. Annex B gives the microbiological sampling-plan interpretation.
Acceptance Criteria: Conformity is based on meeting the requirements in Tables 1–3 and applicable clauses; microbiological results are interpreted using the 2-class/3-class sampling plans in Annex B.
Marking: Package marking includes product/brand name, manufacturer details, material type, batch/code, drying process, manufacture/packing date, net quantity, storage directions, expiry/use-by date, reconstitution directions and applicable regulatory information. Standard Mark may be used for conforming certified products.
Application: Whole milk powder for consumption/use as specified by the product and applicable food regulations.
Evidence / Section: Clause 1, p.1; Clauses 3.1–3.8 and Tables 1–3, pp.3–4; Clauses 4–6, pp.4–6; Annexes B–C, pp.7–10 (PDF pp.3–10).

Title: PACKAGED DRINKING WATER (OTHER THAN PACKAGED NATURAL MINERAL WATER) — SPECIFICATION (First Revision)
Scope: Prescribes requirements and methods of sampling and test for drinking water, other than natural mineral water, offered for sale in packaged form.
Material: Water may originate from potable sources and may undergo filtration, aeration, membrane/depth/cartridge filtration, activated-carbon filtration, demineralization, remineralization, reverse osmosis or other prescribed treatment. Packaging may use PE, PVC, polypropylene, PET/PBT, polycarbonate, polystyrene or suitable sterile glass as specified.
Dimensions: Containers may be of various compositions, forms and capacities suitable for direct consumption; no single dimensional value is specified in the cited scope.
Performance: Microbiological requirements include absence of E. coli, coliforms, faecal streptococci/Staphylococcus aureus, sulphite-reducing anaerobes, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, yeast/mould, Salmonella/Shigella and Vibrio as specified. Physical/chemical requirements include colour max 2 true colour units, turbidity max 2 NTU, TDS max 500 mg/l and pH 6.5–8.5, plus limits in Tables 2–4.
Testing: Tests are specified against the referenced IS methods in Tables 1–4, including microbiological methods and physical/chemical tests such as colour, odour, taste, turbidity, TDS and pH.
Sampling: Representative samples shall be drawn and conformity established according to Annex E.
Acceptance Criteria: Product must comply with the microbiological, physical/chemical, contaminant/toxin, pesticide and other applicable requirements in the standard; conformity is established using Annex E.
Marking: Label should state product name, processor name/address, brand (if any), batch/code, processing/packing date, disinfection treatment (if any), best-before information, net volume, storage direction and applicable statutory markings. Medicinal/curative claims are prohibited.
Application: Packaged drinking water offered for sale for direct consumption, other than packaged natural mineral water.
Evidence / Section: Clause 1, p.1; Clauses 3.2 and 5.1–5.2, pp.1–3; Tables 1–4; Clauses 6–8, pp.3–4 (PDF pp.19–22).
